title: Unit – 4 : Session – 8 : SLO – 1  |  Micro-programmed Control — Match the Following
sections: 1. Microinstruction — A. Contains all control signals for one clock cycle.
2. Control Store — C. ROM storing microprograms.
3. Nanocode — B. Breaks microinstructions into smaller steps (a second, finer level of control encoding).
5. Horizontal Microcode — F. Each bit directly controls a signal (wide words, no decoding).
6. Vertical Microcode — D. Uses multiple microinstruction formats (short, encoded words needing decoders).
7. Micro-PC — G. Points to the next microinstruction.
8. Emulation — H. Imitating complex instructions (one machine imitating another's ISA via microcode).
9. Dynamic Microprogramming — I. Modifiable control store (writable control store).
10. Microsequencer — J. Decides the next microinstruction address.
